title: PDUNASS Inaugurates Joint EPFO–ITC-ILO Training Programme on “Actuarial Practices in Social Security: Strengthening Actuarial Governance at EPFO India”
body_text:
The Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya National Academy of Social Security (PDUNASS) inaugurated the residential phase of a specialized training programme titled “Actuarial Practices in Social Security: Strengthening Actuarial Governance at EPFO India” on 10th August in New Delhi .
Organized jointly by the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) and the International Training Centre of the International Labour Organization (ITC-ILO), the three-day residential phase (10–12 August 2026) follows a comprehensive online module conducted via the ITC-ILO e-Campus from 25 May to 9 August 2026.
Welcoming the Chief Guest and the ILO/ITC-ILO delegation, Shri Kumar Rohit, Director, PDUNASS, noted that the initiative aligns with PDUNASS’s mandate as EPFO’s apex training institute to bring internationally benchmarked learning to its officers. Expressing gratitude for the strategic partnership, he remarked:"With the EPF, EPS, and EDLI schemes aligning with the Code on Social Security, 2020, strengthening in-house actuarial capacity is both timely and essential."
Mr. Oktavianto Pasaribu, Deputy Director and Senior Advisor for Regional Partnership and Resource Mobilization, ILO, highlighted that the collaboration reflects the ILO’s commitment to strengthening social protection systems across South Asia. He emphasized that sound actuarial governance is central to the financial sustainability of social security institutions and commended EPFO’s proactive approach to building in-house capacity.
Presenting an overview of the curriculum, Mr. Charles Crevier, ITC-ILO Faculty, outlined the blended structure of the programme and the key residential themes, which include:
Actuarial valuation methods Asset-Liability Management (ALM) Global best governance practices in social security institutions
Delivering the keynote address and formally declaring the programme inaugurated, Shri Ramesh Krishnamurthi, Central Provident Fund Commissioner ( CPFC), observed that as custodian of retirement savings, pensions, and insurance for crores of workers, every actuarial decision at EPFO impacts the financial security of millions. He urged officers to elevate actuarial work into a strategic governance function and foster an evidence-based culture across EPFO."As EPFO continues to grow in size and responsibility, strengthening our actuarial capacity becomes increasingly important to strengthen governance and prepare better for future challenges." Said Shri Ramesh Krishnamurthi, CPFC .
The inaugural session and residential phase were attended by senior leadership and operational officers, including:
Financial Adviser & Chief Accounts Officer (FA & CAO), ACCs, RPFC-Is, RPFC-IIs, SOs, and ASOs from EPFO Representatives and officials from ESIC Other prominent experts present included Mr. Amjad Rabi (ITC-ILO Faculty), Ms. Divya Verma (Senior Programme Officer, ILO), and Mr. Karun Gopinath (National Project Coordinator, ILO).
About PDUNASS
The Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya National Academy of Social Security (PDUNASS) is the apex training and research institute of the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), functioning under the Ministry of Labour & Employment, Government of India. Established in 1990, PDUNASS is dedicated to training, research, and consultancy in social security administration.
About ITC-ILO
The International Training Centre of the International Labour Organization (ITC-ILO), based in Turin, Italy, is the training arm of the ILO. It designs and delivers capacity-building programmes for ILO constituents worldwide—including governments, employers’ and workers’ organisations—in areas central to promoting decent work, social protection, and social security governance.

enrichment.summary: PDUNASS, EPFO's apex training institute, inaugurated a joint EPFO–ITC-ILO residential training programme on actuarial governance in New Delhi on 10 August 2026. The three-day residential phase (10-12 August 2026) follows an online module run via ITC-ILO e-Campus from 25 May to 9 August 2026, covering actuarial valuation methods, Asset-Liability Management, and global governance best practices. The programme was inaugurated by CPFC Shri Ramesh Krishnamurthi and attended by senior EPFO and ESIC officials along with ILO/ITC-ILO faculty.
enrichment.context:
EPFO manages retirement savings, pension, and insurance schemes (EPF, EPS, EDLI) for a very large workforce in India, making sound actuarial valuation critical to the financial sustainability of these funds. The Code on Social Security, 2020 seeks to consolidate and modernize India's social security framework, including provisions relevant to EPFO's schemes, increasing the need for robust in-house actuarial and governance capacity. This training reflects a broader trend of Indian social security institutions partnering with international bodies like the ILO to benchmark practices against global standards, particularly as India's social protection net expands under codes like the Code on Social Security, 2020 and schemes covering an increasingly large and diverse workforce, including gig and platform workers.

PDUNASS, established in 1990, serves as EPFO's research and training arm, while ITC-ILO (Turin) is the ILO's global capacity-building institution. Such collaborations are part of India's engagement with ILO on decent work and social protection agendas, and also signal EPFO's institutional efforts to strengthen governance, transparency, and evidence-based decision-making as it scales up its responsibilities.

options: Ministry of Labour & Employment via executive order
prelims_questions.explanation: The Code on Social Security, 2020 is a Parliamentary enactment that consolidates multiple labour laws related to social security, including those governing EPFO's schemes, as referenced in the release.

prelims_questions.question: PDUNASS, EPFO's apex training and research institute mentioned in the release, is named after which leader and was established in which year?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states PDUNASS stands for Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya National Academy of Social Security and was established in 1990.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of actuarial governance for the long-term financial sustainability of India's social security institutions like EPFO. In this context, examine how the Code on Social Security, 2020 seeks to strengthen social protection architecture in India.

International collaborations, such as those between EPFO and the ILO, are increasingly used to build institutional capacity in India's social security administration. Critically analyze the role of such partnerships in improving governance standards in public welfare institutions.
